1 Fractional distillation and cracking are important steps in processing crude oil.
(a) Place ticks ( ) in the columns to show which statements apply to each step. You may place a tick in one column, in both columns or in neither column.
(b) The formula CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3 represents one of the compounds in crude oil.
(i) Give the molecular formula of this compound.
(ii) Give the displayed formula of this compound.
(iii) Give the empirical formula of this compound.
(iv) Give the name of this compound.
(v) Give the general formula of the homologous series that contains this compound.
(c) The products of the complete combustion of hydrocarbons are carbon dioxide and water.
(i) Bal e the equation to show the complete combustion of ethene (C2H4).
(ii) Draw a dot and cross diagram to show the bonding in an ethene molecule.
Show only the outer electrons in each atom.
(d) Ethanol can be manufactured by the hydration of ethene. The equation for this reaction is
C2H4(g) + H2O(g) → C2H5OH(g)
(i) Identify the catalyst and state the temperature used in this process.
(ii) A 20 mol sample of ethanol was produced using this reaction.
Deduce the amount, in moles, of ethene needed and the volume, in dm3, that this amount of ethene would occupy at room temperature and pressure.
Assume that all of the ethene is converted into ethanol and that the molar volume of ethene is 24 dm3 at rtp.
(separate only)

3 Ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon.
(a) (i) The molecular formula of ethene is
A CH4
B C2H6
C C2H4
D C3H6
(ii) Ethene is bubbled into bromine water until there is no further change.
(iii) Ethene can be formed from ethanol.
This type of reaction is called
A dehydration
B oxidation
C reduction
D substitution
(b) This apparatus can be used to decompose decane (C10H22).
ceramic wool soaked in decane
porous pot
heat heat
gas mixture containing ethene
water
(i) What name is given to this type of thermal decomposition?
(ii) Porous pot contains oxides such as silica and alumina. What is the purpose of the porous pot in this experiment?
(iii) Suggest why the gas collected is a mixture and not pure ethene.
(Total for Question 3 = 6 marks)
4 (a) Ethanol can be manufactured by two different processes.
stage 1 stage 2 glucose ethanol
Process 11 sucrose ethanol Process 22 ethene
(i) What is the general name for compounds such as sucrose and glucose?
(ii) What type of reaction occurs in stage 2?
(iii) What is the catalyst used in stage 2?
(iv) What type of reaction occurs in process 2?
(b) The table shows the displayed formulae of four organic compounds.
Ethanol and compound D are members of the homologous series of alcohols.
(i) The first member of this homologous series is methanol.
(ii) Suggest the name of compound D.

(c) In industry, the conversion of propene to compound D uses the same conditions as those used in the conversion of ethene to ethanol. Identify a suitable catalyst and temperature for these conversions.
(d) Ethene and acetylene can both be used for welding metals.
The equations for the reactions of these gases in welding are ethene acetylene
C2H4 + 3O2 2CO2 + 2H2O C2H2 + 2.5O2 2CO2 + H2O
One problem with using hydrocarbons as fuels is incomplete combustion. (i) Incomplete combustion is a bigger problem with ethene than with acetylene.
Suggest why.
(ii) One of the gases produced during incomplete combustion is dangerous to humans. Identify this gas and explain how it is dangerous.
(e) Ethene can be used to ripen bananas.
Bananas are placed in a large container and ethene is added. The ethene can be added in two different ways.
(i) In method 1, ethene is stored under pressure and passed through a pipe into the container. Suggest one risk in using this method.
(ii) In method 2, the generator contains a known quantity of ethanol that is slowly decomposed to ethene using a catalyst. Write a chemical equation for this decomposition.
(Total for Question 4 = 14 marks)
5 An industrial chemical company has supplies of ethene and ethanol.
The company considers using these two processes.
process 1 converting ethene to ethanol
process 2 converting ethanol to ethene
A chemical equation for process 1 is
C2H4 + H2O C2H6O
(a) Which condition does the chemical company use in process 1?
(b) The equation for process 1 shows the molecular formulae of ethene and ethanol.
(c) Why is it correct to describe ethanol as saturated, but incorrect to describe it as a hydrocarbon?
(d) A scientist working for the chemical company makes the following predictions that could affect processes 1 and 2 in the future:
crude oil will be less available and more expensive the climate will be warmer and allow more sugar cane to be grown
Suggest how each of these predictions would affect the two processes.
(Total for Question 5 = 8 marks)
